conventions: `εὐαγγελίζομαι` is rendered *preach the gospel* and the whole phrase belongs to that one verb token (9:16 twice, 9:18). At 9:18 `τὸ εὐαγγέλιον` also stands as a separate object and takes its own *the gospel*, so the same two English words answer to different tokens in one verse. Rule 103's test is licensing and not recurrence, and neither occurrence is `added`.

Interrogative `μή` opening the rhetorical questions of 9:4, 9:5, 9:8 and 9:9 is `unrepresented` throughout under rule 44, the ASV marking each by inversion alone. At 9:9 the inversion is the cleft *Is it … that*, and that frame is the impersonal `μέλει`'s own English rather than a supplied interrogative word, so it does not bring the particle back under rule 44's second arm.

An article governing a substantival adjective or quantifier takes the supplied generic nominal even where the ASV writes no determiner, with the case preposition riding along, and leaves the adjective or quantifier bare: `τὰ πνευματικά` -> *things* / *spiritual* and `τὰ σαρκικά` -> *things* / *carnal* at 9:11, `τὰ ἱερά` -> *things* / *sacred* at 9:13, `τοῖς πᾶσιν` -> *to … men* / *all* at 9:22. Anarthrous Greek is the contrast and keeps the nominal on the quantifier itself, `πάντα` -> *all things* at 9:12, 9:22 and 9:23 and `πάντων` -> *all men* at 9:19, and 9:22 writes both halves in one verse.

Two supplied English words in this chapter are `added` and every other one folds. 9:10's italic *to thresh* is `added` because `ἀλοῶν` is already spent on *thresheth* (rule 103), and 9:13's italic *and* is `added` because it seams two finite clauses the Greek left asyndetic and neither is a participle converted to a finite clause (rule 98, not rule 88). Where a supplied word instead completes a token's own unfinished English it folds: *the corn* on `ἀλοῶντα` at 9:9, *men* on `πάντων` at 9:19, *in the games* on `ἀγωνιζόμενος` and *do it* on `ἐκεῖνοι` at 9:25, *this* on `τῆς` at 9:12 and *it were* on `καλόν` at 9:15. Rule 11 keeps the italics from deciding either way.
report: Checked all 51 candidate lemma groups and read the full dump end to end for the splits the table is blind to (supplied English marked `added` in one verse and folded in another). No construction is analysed two ways without something in the source licensing the difference, so no patches.

Article plus substantival adjective or quantifier: 9:11 (twice), 9:13 and 9:22 all give the supplied nominal (*things*, *men*) and any case preposition to the article and leave the adjective or quantifier bare, while the anarthrous quantifiers at 9:12, 9:19, 9:22, 9:23 and 9:25 keep the nominal themselves. 9:22 writes both halves in one verse, so it reads like a split and is exactly rule 102's contrast.

Supplied predicate in a clause with no predicate: 9:12 `ἡμεῖς` -> *do we* and 9:25 `ἐκεῖνοι` -> *they do it* are parallel and both put the supplied verb on the subject under rules 56 and 68. Not a split.

`οὕτως` takes *Even so* headed on *so* at 9:14 and 9:24 and a bare *so* at 9:15 and 9:26 where the ASV writes no correlative; `καί` is `unrepresented` at 9:14 under rule 100 and takes *even* at 9:5 under rule 82's bare-*even* clause, where no *so* competes. `ἵνα` -> *to* at 9:25 against *that* elsewhere is rule 40's own case.

BSB disagreements: none is a genuine error. The five PRT-N are four interrogative `μή` (9:4, 9:5, 9:8, 9:9) under rule 44 and one redundant `οὐ` (9:15) under rule 41, and both rules say in terms that the report is not a correction. 9:12 `τοῦ` before `Χριστοῦ` has no English determiner to anchor, so rule 23 empties it and rule 21 leaves *of* on the name. 9:14 `καί` is rule 100. No accepted edge was changed.

Both `added` units survive review: 9:10 *to thresh* (rule 103, `ἀλοῶν` already spent on *thresheth*) and 9:13 *and* (rule 98, an asyndetic seam between two like clauses, neither a participle converted to a finite clause, so rule 88 does not reach it). Every other supplied word in the chapter has an unspent licensing token and folds.

Hedged edges left standing, each naming its competing reading in its own note: the `κατά` frame head at 9:8 (rule 67's standing division for a proper preposition), `εἰς` -> *so as* headed on *so* at 9:18 (heading on *as* as the complementizer is defensible), `πάντως` -> *by all means* at 9:22, `μή` -> *to forbear* at 9:6, `οὐκ` -> *nothing* at 9:16, and the supplied *of the* on `ἀπόστολοι` at 9:5.
